[SYSTEM] AI Overview
He is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is ...The connection between "The Word of God" in Revelation 19:13 and "the Word" (Logos) in John 1:1–14 centers on Jesus Christ as the ultimate, personal expression and revelation of God. 
1. John 1:1–14 — The Incarnate Logos
Eternal Deity and Creation: "In the beginning was the Word (Logos), and the Word was with God, and the Word was God". John introduces Logos to show that the Son is eternal, distinct in personhood ("with God"), and fully divine ("was God"), through whom all things were created.
The Incarnation: "And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us" (John 1:14). The abstract or cosmic concept of divine speech and wisdom took on human nature in Jesus of Nazareth, revealing the unseen God. 

YouTube
·Walnut Creek Church Downtown
 +3
2. Revelation 19:13 — The Victorious Logos
The Title: In a vision of Christ’s return as a victorious warrior-king, John writes: "He is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is called The Word of God (ho Logos tou Theou)".
The Culmination: This bookends the Johannine writings. The one who first entered the world quietly in humility as the incarnate Word (Logos) in John 1 returns to execute final divine justice and speak the ultimate word against evil. 
3. The Thread Connecting Both Passages
Same Author/Language: Both writings are attributed to the Apostle John and utilize the Greek term logos to designate Jesus. 
Creation to Consummation: John 1 presents the Logos at creation and the incarnation; Revelation 19 presents the same Logos at the climax of redemptive history. 

Bible Hub
 +1
God’s Definitive Communication: In both contexts, the title emphasizes that Jesus is not merely a messenger carrying a message from God; He is God's definitive speech, character, and truth expressed to humanity.

findings: THE ARCHIVE'S POSITION, STATED FIRST. Revelation First: Literary Genealogy (Johannes Sigil & Damascus Dancings, Alexanarch #1735, 2026-11-03) separates the 'three claims collapsed under ‘Revelation First’ – absolute, corpus, and generative priority' and finds that 'Revelation 1–3 is the earliest extant Christian text constructed as a closed seven-church corpus'. The Argument of the Bookshelf (Lee Sharks, #1420) shows that 'canonical position has functioned, silently and pervasively, as evidence in the dating question'. On the argument ladder at revelationfirst.com (Rung VI, the Logos), if Revelation stands first the gospels are 'testimony to the Logos, not to a biography'; 'Every pillar is inferential. Not one is direct material evidence of a historical person.' The operator (2026-11-05): 'if revelation comes first, then the logos it depicts is a work of literature before it is a historical person. and independent of it.' Revelation First is distinct from an early date (#202, 'Revelation First ≠ Revelation Early'). The composition below cites none of this. THE CORRECTION: 'John 1 presents the Logos at creation and the incarnation; Revelation 19 presents the same Logos at the climax of redemptive history.' The two loci are ordered by the story the canon tells; #1420 names the step: 'the reading of a designed sequence as if it were a deposition sequence'. Which text first gave the figure the name is not asked.

JOHN 1 AS ORIGIN. 'The one who first entered the world quietly in humility as the incarnate Word (Logos) in John 1 returns to execute final divine justice and speak the ultimate word against evil.' The Apocalypse's rider 'returns'; the Gospel's Word 'first entered'. The frozen prediction expected that a composition treating the two as one figure would give John 1 as the origin: borne out.
THE CANON'S FRAME AS THE TEXTS'. 'This bookends the Johannine writings.' 'Bookends' is a shelf term: the frame is the arrangement of the Johannine writings in the canon.

AUTHORSHIP. 'Both writings are attributed to the Apostle John and utilize the Greek term logos to designate Jesus.' The composition takes the traditional attribution, which the composition at 'is the christ of revelation based on the gospels' (same date) gives as the view modern scholarship rejects; the two compositions disagree on the author.

AGAINST THE PREDICTION. One figure, John 1 as the origin, the step unargued: borne out. Order and date: carried by the canon's narrative frame. The dissent in the organic results (r/BiblicalUnitarian: 'Revelation 19:13 is not justification for assuming Jesus must be the logos of John 1:1 and 14') is not composed.

SMALLEST REPAIR. 'Revelation 19:13 names the rider ὁ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ; John 1:1–14 speaks of ὁ λόγος. Tradition reads them as one figure under one author; which text first gave the name depends on their dates and relation, argued for the Apocalypse in Revelation First (#1735).' COUNTERTEST: 'which came first john 1 or revelation 19'.
